newsitem.title: USA: New York State plans to sell $4.7 bln debt in Q4.
newsitem.headline: New York State plans to sell $4.7 bln debt in Q4.

text.p: New York state, its agencies, and New York City plan to sell about $4.7 billion of debt in the fourth quarter, the state comptroller said Tuesday.
When broken down by month, the sale schedule shows that most of the offerings are concentrated in October, when $2.9 billion of offerings are expected.
In November, almost $1.4 billion is expected to be sold, while in December the total is $458 million.
The list of borrowings released by state comptroller H. Carl McCall included:
--New York State, $107 million sale of Certificates of Participation in November.
--New York City, $500 million bond sale and a $1.515 billion of revenue anticipation notes in October.
--New York Housing Development Corp, bond sales of $17 million and $53 million in November, followed by a $57 million bond sale in December.
--New York City Water Authority, $200 million bond sale in October.
